newsitem.title: SYRIA: Radical Palestinians vow to wreck Israel-PLO deal.
newsitem.headline: Radical Palestinians vow to wreck Israel-PLO deal.

text.p: Radical Palestinian guerrilla groups on Thursday condemned the terms of a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron as a crime against Palestinians and vowed to wreck the accord.

The 10-member alliance, which claimed responsibility for several suicide bombings against Israel since its peace agreement with the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993, said the new accord met all Israel's conditions.

"Like the previous treacherous deals, this accord does not represent our people or reflect its will. The alliance will continue its struggle and jihad (holy war) to foil it and the deals of capitulation and surrender," the statement said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat ended months of negotiations on Wednesday by signing a deal that will leave Israel in control of 20 percent of Hebron to protect Jewish settlers.
The alliance condemned Arafat for the deal, which is said let Netanyahu "beautify his ugly face and appear as a man of peace after his policies were condemned by the world."

The Damascus-based alliance groups Islamic fundamentalist groups Hamas and Islamic Jihad and marxist factions including the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) and the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP).
"The Palestinian alliance holds Arafat's Authority and some Arab regimes which exerted efforts to conclude it responsible for imposing it on the Palestinians," it added.
The Hebron agreement followed mediation by King Hussein of Jordan, who consulted Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak as well as Arafat and Netanyahu before the accord emerged.

Some of the Damascus-based groups have strong support inside the West Bank and Gaza Strip. They have constantly opposed the PLO-Israeli peace process, which has given Palestinians limited self-rule over parts of the West Bank and Gaza -- far less than Arafat had once demanded.

"Arafat's (Palestinian) Authority has committed a new crime against our Palestinian people and Arab and Islamic nation through its surrender to Netanyahu's conditions for redeployment in Hebron," the statement said.
"This accord will increase the possibility of the launching of aggressive military actions against Syria and Lebanon by the Zionist entity," the statement said.
"It will also increase American pressure and threats of blockade against Syria and Lebanon to force them to change their position, which is rejecting capitulation," the statement added.

The statement said the Hebron accord had accepted that Netanyahu, elected last May, was not bound by agreements signed by the previous Israeli government. "This will allow the enemy to extend this principle on all other tracks of the negotiations," it said.
